The Senior AI Adoption Lead takes ownership of ALK's continuous AI adoption programme, turning enthusiasm into real, safe, everyday value from the AI tools available to ALK employees. This role continues the adoption efforts from 2025 (over 1,000 employees trained in GenAI usage) and 2026 (more tailored training on ALK's AI solutions) and is key to achieving ALK's AI ambition within the Allergy+ strategy.

This role requires genuine enthusiasm for enabling people, facilitating great learning experiences, and driving change. The Senior AI Adoption Lead must work closely with people across all business areas, be proactive, reach out to employees, and drive AI adoption across the entire organization so that the change is permanent and sticks with employees.

This role owns ALK's continuous AI adoption programme, covering general enablement on GenAI, tailored upskilling for all employees, and engagement activities that drive adoption. This includes preparing and hosting AI training (both general-purpose and tool-specific), the training calendar, micro-learning, maintaining AI at ALK intranet site. The role also owns measuring GenAI usage across the organization, providing the data needed to support informed decisions in AI strategy implementation.

This is not an engineering role – the person does not need to build or configure AI solutions. It does, however, require basic understanding of both business and IT, so the Senior AI Adoption Lead can act as an effective bridge between the two. Genuine enthusiasm for new technologies, especially generative AI, is required. Experience with usage of those technologies in daily life and enterprise scenario is vital.

The Senior AI Adoption Lead acts as a proxy between business and IT: translating technical concepts into everyday business language, aligning business demand with IT delivery, triaging common issues, and accelerating adoption before escalation to IT.

This role is based in Denmark, where ALK has its headquarters and the majority of AI users. It also requires occasional business travel to conduct in-person workshops and training.

Major fields of responsibility:

• 
Communicate the need for AI adoption through meetings, newsletters, MS Teams, and Intranet; share success stories, best practices, and enthusiasm for upcoming initiatives.

• 
Foster engagement through targeted workshops for departments and business units, regular manager briefings, tailored communications, and a visible emphasis on the benefits of AI in daily work.

• 
Map use cases and design training courses (e.g. Foundations, Advanced Prompting, Leading with GenAI) and micro-learning, and activate and coordinate a network of AI Champions to extend reach.

• 
Provide accessible, tiered learning resources through the AI community and Learning Hub (Teams channel, SharePoint) — videos, live webinars, in-person workshops, quick-start guides, FAQs, and playbooks.

• 
Support enterprise-AI pilots with onboarding, enablement and value evaluation; collect feedback and resolve common non-technical issues; and maintain a tight feedback loop with IT on platform updates, governance, and support to keep adoption aligned and safe.

• 
Work side by side with the technical teams (programmers, architects, data and platform specialists): take part in solution and roadmap discussions, learn how the solutions work, ask questions from the end-user perspective, challenge and advise on usability, and translate the outcome into layman terms for the business.

• 
Define and measure adoption rates and satisfaction (usage, surveys, focus groups) and report impact to leadership; run iterative cycles to refine training content based on user feedback and business priorities; and recognize high adopters through awards and acknowledgment.

Qualifications:

• 
Minimum 10 years' experience in change management, IT systems adoption, and training management and delivery

• 
Proven facilitation, training and change-management experience

• 
Outstanding communication and stakeholder skills across all levels

• 
Fluent in English.

• 
Hands-on curiosity about generative AI

• 
Practical experience with creation of AI assistants (e.g. custom skills in Anthropic Claude or custom agents in M365 Copilot).

• 
Analytical mindset able to translate adoption data into actionable insights.

• 
Self-driven, organized and creative, comfortable working across business and IT**.**

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Financial Analyst, you'll own the day-to-day financial planning and analysis (FP&A) across clinical programmes, research and corporate functions. You'll turn financial data and input from colleagues into reliable forecasts, useful insights and clear reporting that helps Hemab make informed decisions.

Working closely with the FP&A Director, you'll take ownership of recurring financial activities while helping build practical ways of working as Hemab grows. Your work will give our teams greater financial clarity and help us make thoughtful decisions about the resources behind our science.

What you'll do

• Own monthly FP&A activities across assigned clinical studies, research projects and functions, keeping forecasts accurate and up to date.

• Partner with functional leads and project teams to understand spending, challenge assumptions and identify financial risks and opportunities early.

• Coordinate quarterly forecasts and contribute to the annual Investment Plan and Long-Range Plan.

• Analyse actuals against forecasts, explain variances and turn financial information into clear, useful insights.

• Prepare management reporting, financial commentary and decision materials for review by the FP&A Director.

• Maintain and improve Power BI reporting, ensuring reliable data and consistent financial information.

• Manage routine financial follow-up with CROs and vendors, including invoice reviews, change orders and financial input to negotiations.

• Build straightforward financial frameworks and reporting practices that help teams work efficiently as Hemab grows.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Experience in FP&A, forecasting, management reporting and financial business partnering.

• Strong financial analysis skills, with the ability to turn complex information into practical recommendations.

• Advanced Excel skills and hands-on experience with Power BI.

• Experience managing forecasts independently, identifying material changes and knowing when to escalate.

• Ability to work effectively with finance and non-finance colleagues, communicate clearly and challenge assumptions constructively.

• Professional fluency in English.

Nice to have

• Experience in biotech, pharma, clinical development, CROs or another project-driven environment.

• Familiarity with clinical study budgets, vendor financial management or financial planning systems.

• Experience improving financial reporting or building ways of working in a growing organisation.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

We value people who take ownership, solve problems, ask for help when needed and work without ego. At our size, how you work matters as much as your CV. Good structure should help people move faster and trust the numbers, not slow them down.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

Regulation & business development

Governance & culture

• You own our whistleblower scheme and case handling.

What we offer

About kompasbank

Europe runs on small and medium-sized businesses. SMEs make up 99% of all EU companies, employ around 100 million people and generate more than half of Europe’s GDP. Yet they are the part of the economy that the financial system serves worst: too complex for automated retail credit, too small to be worth a traditional corporate bank’s attention. The Draghi report on European competitiveness was blunt. Europe is falling behind the US and China in growth, productivity and technology, and fragmented, slow-moving capital is a central reason why. Europe will not become relevant again through a handful of champions alone. It needs thousands of ambitious mid-sized companies that can get financing, move money domestically and internationally, and scale across borders as easily as their American competitors. That is where kompasbank stands. Built on a full EU banking licence, we bank European SMEs properly, with serious service, data excellence and the regulatory rigour that lets us say yes where others say no.

We’re a cloud-native neobank with no legacy systems and no silos. Phanofi is a DTU spin-out building the next generation of optical communication infrastructure. We design integrated photonic interconnect chips that reduce power consumption and increase data throughput for AI datacenters, quantum computing, and space applications.

As a diverse team of 16, we are at an inflection point, growing our engineering capability to take our photonic interconnect technology from prototype toward scalable, production-ready products.
